So, US military policy, at least in the Marines was similar to this. Every Physical Fitness Test (PFT) or Combat Fitness Test (CFT) you get height and weight checked. Its supposed to work out such that you do 1 PFT and 1 CFT for score a year. Realistically you'll be lucky if you're running one only every three months. I had one unit we did a PFT every week at one point. Even though only one a year is for score they'd typically weigh us in every PFT.

So, if you weighed in over your max weight you'd have to get "tapped' (having your body fat measured by a ratio of the measurements between your neck and waist). If you're fat it's typically obvious and known but still procedure is a big thing for the Corps obviously.

If you weigh in over, and tape in at your company over your BF% you get sent to Battalion (basically just next level of authority) and they do the same weigh & measure and tell you you're fat. After this you have to go to medical to ensure you don't have some legit disorder like actual thyroid shit or something. Then when that comes back negative you typically will get measured & taped one last time. Then the fun begins.

If after all this you are still fat, you're officially fat and put on Body Composition Platoon (BCP) you PT with a group of other fatties twice a day, you're supposed to eat less at the chow hall and you're weighed like weekly.
